reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 blind reviewer, re-review after the distance-clause fixes, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm. The distance from the gate to the tree is 20 cm. Which distance is longer?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Which is longer: 14 cm or 17 cm?
Which is longer: 9 cm or 14 cm?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Which is longer: 16 cm or 9 cm?
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
Which is longer: 409 cm or 237 cm?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 347 cm. The distance from the gate to the tree is 164 cm. Which distance is longer?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 278 cm. The distance from the gate to the tree is 206 cm. Which distance is longer?
Which is longer: 9 cm or 12 cm?
A garden path is 30 cm long. A crayon is 7 cm long. How many cm longer is a garden path than a crayon?
Which is longer: 13 cm or 6 cm?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ m.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sentence names three things: measuring object length, comparing lengths, and distance in meters. The first two are met - seed 43 gives 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' and seed 44 gives 'Which is longer: 14 cm or 17 cm?' - but the distance clause is rendered in the wrong unit in every distance seed. Seed 42 states 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm.' and seed 501 states 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 347 cm.', so no seed in this packet expresses a distance in meters, which is the only unit the competency allows for distance.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Taking each named part separately: measuring an object is covered (seeds 43, 46, 55, 603); comparing lengths is covered (seeds 44, 45, 50, 600, 602); centimeters are covered everywhere; meters appear in exactly one of fourteen samples, seed 603 with 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ m.'; distance in meters is not covered at all, only distance stated in cm. The measuring-tool part is likewise unrepresented, since seed 55 asks 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.' and seed 43 opens with 'Measure the object.', naming neither the object nor any ruler or meter stick in the rendered stem.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Load is right for Grade 2 Quarter 2. Comparisons are single binary reads of two whole numbers, and the one multi-step item, seed 601 asking 'How many cm longer is a garden path than a crayon?' with answer 23, is a single subtraction. The largest quantities, 409 and 347, stay inside the Grade 2 whole-number range, and every stem is one or two short sentences with four options.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct item shapes appear across the fourteen seeds: direct measurement read-off at seed 46 with 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.', two-length comparison at seed 602 with 'Which is longer: 13 cm or 6 cm?', two-distance comparison at seed 502, and a difference item at seed 601. Three formatters are exercised (mcq, cloze, read_mcq). Worth noting but not blocking: the distance items all reuse one frame, 'The distance from the gate to the tree is', with only the numerals changing across seeds 42, 501 and 502.

competency_alignment.rationale: The distance sub-case is aligned to the wrong unit. The competency confines distance to meters, yet seed 502 renders 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 278 cm.' and seed 42 renders 'The distance from the gate to the tree is 20 cm.' The object-length items align correctly and nothing reaches past the competency into area or unit conversion, but no stem invokes the measuring tool the competency names: seed 43 asks for a measurement with 'Measure the object.' and no instrument in the text.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Several magnitudes are not ones a child could plausibly measure with the implied tool. Seed 42 places two outdoor landmarks a pencil-length apart with 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm.', and seed 601 offers 'A garden path is 30 cm long.', a path shorter than a school ruler. Seed 500 asks 'Which is longer: 409 cm or 237 cm?', expressing lengths of over four and over two meters in centimeters, which is not what a Grade 2 child reads off a cm ruler.
